findings.title: Blacklist and duplicate checks are case-sensitive, so they can be bypassed.
findings.body: The blacklist is lowercased but `guest` is not. Entering `Bad@Example.com` gets past a blacklist entry `bad@example.com`. The attendee check is also an exact string match, so `John@x.com` is added again next to `john@x.com`. The server schema does not reject duplicates within one request either; only the client does. A direct call with `[a, a]` inserts two identical attendees. Normalize to lowercase and dedupe on the server before filtering.

findings.title: Emails use the raw `guests` list instead of the filtered `uniqueGuests`.
findings.body: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` decides who counts as new from the unfiltered input. If the request includes an email that was already an attendee, that person gets a fresh 'scheduled' email instead of the 'guests added' notice. Pass `uniqueGuests`.

findings.title: Guests can be added to cancelled, rejected or past bookings.
findings.body: Nothing checks the booking status or end time. Adding guests to a cancelled booking still writes attendees, calls the calendar update and sends emails with `status: "CONFIRMED"` ICS files. The new guests are invited to a meeting that does not exist. Reject bookings that are not accepted/pending or that have already ended.

findings.title: Team admin/owner check uses && so only owners get through.
findings.body: `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)` is true only when the user passes both checks. In practice that means team owners. A team ADMIN who is not the organizer or an attendee gets FORBIDDEN. This assumes `isTeamAdmin` matches ADMIN (and maybe OWNER) and `isTeamOwner` matches OWNER only; I could not see either function. Use `||`, or just `isTeamAdmin` if it already covers owners.

findings.title: No cap on the number of guests, and any attendee can add them, so this can be abused to send email spam.
findings.body: Any attendee of a booking can call this mutation (authorization includes `isAttendee`). The guest array is unbounded, and every new guest gets a platform-sent invitation with an ICS file. Someone who books a public event can send mass mail from the Cal.com domain to arbitrary addresses. Add `.max(n)` and a unique refinement to the schema, and consider rate limiting or restricting this to organizers/admins.

findings.title: The fallback error message can never show, and the error banner is never cleared on success.
findings.body: `message` is a template string that is never empty, so `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` never applies. When `err.data` is missing the user sees `undefined: ...`. Separately, `isInvalidEmail` is only reset by Cancel. After a failed validation and then a successful add, the stale error shows the next time the dialog opens. Reset it in `onSuccess` and build the message conditionally.
